theories.claim: handleSprintQAEvidence, handleSprintQAAdjudication, handleSprintQAIssues, handleSprintQAIssue, handleSprintQAAssessment, and handleSprintQASmokeSuite all type-assert h.qa to app.QAEvidenceQueries (qa_handlers.go:24,38,52,75,89,103); if the adapter behind h.qa only implements the older QAQueries interface, all six endpoints return ErrWebUnavailable and the Sprint 37 evidence surface is unreachable through the web boundary.
theories.basis: Cross-package contract between internal/web and internal/app: qa_handlers.go depends on the additive app.QAEvidenceQueries interface (sprint_usecases.go:87-96) that adds QAEvidence, QAAdjudication, QAIssues, QAIssue, QAAssessment, and QASmokeSuite on top of the base QAQueries. docs/architecture.md states the web layer receives only the closed operation capability supplied by the composition root and must not decide workflow semantics; the additive interface is the documented extension point.
theories.confirmation_condition: Static reading shows qa_handlers.go makes six QAEvidenceQueries type assertions that all return ErrWebUnavailable on failure; sprint_usecases.go:87-96 declares the additive interface and dashboardUseCases implements all six methods (lines 802,819,837,890,909,929).
theories.refutation_condition: Type assertions match a single concrete adapter that always implements the additive surface, OR the composition root injects an adapter that satisfies the union of QAQueries and QAEvidenceQueries.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Static reading alone cannot confirm which concrete adapter is injected into h.qa at composition time.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: grep -n "func (u dashboardUseCases) QA" internal/app/sprint_usecases.go and grep -n "QAEvidenceQueries" internal/app/*.go internal/web/*.go to enumerate every implementation and consumer; confirm the injection site binds the union interface.
theories.outcome_reason: Cross-package contract is textually present and the additive interface comment matches the architecture description, but the composition-time binding of h.qa cannot be verified from these read-only context paths.

theories.claim: buildQAEvidencePublication admits evidence only when pprocess.IsolationCapabilityFacts returns NativeProtectedRootDeny AND DescendantCleanup AND WorkspaceRemoval all true (qa.go:463), and the admission struct is validated by ValidateQAAdmission before any evidence plan is frozen.
theories.basis: docs/architecture.md (QA evidence and isolation) states writable checks get a new 0700 non-Git-dependent copy, bubblewrap mounts the host root read-only and remounts only the disposable copy writable, and platforms that cannot prove protected-root denial, process-group cleanup, and workspace removal report the missing capability and QA blocks before writable work. qa.go:458-468 materializes those facts through pprocess.IsolationCapabilityFacts() and binds them into admission.IsolationProven.
theories.verification_surface: internal/sprint/qa.go:449-468, internal/platform/process/isolation.go:38-46, docs/architecture.md (QA evidence and isolation section)
theories.confirmation_condition: Reading the three capability names in admission.IsolationProven matches exactly the three capability names architecture.md lists for platform gating; ValidateQAAdmission is invoked and any false capability blocks evidence publication.
theories.refutation_condition: ValidateQAAdmission treats IsolationProven as advisory rather than blocking, OR the three names in code do not equal the three names in architecture.md.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Static reading cannot exercise ValidateQAAdmission with each capability toggled off.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: grep -n "IsolationProven\|ValidateQAAdmission" internal/sprint/*.go to enumerate every site that interprets the three capabilities, and read ValidateQAAdmission source.
theories.outcome_reason: Names and gating presence are textually consistent across both packages; runtime consequence of a missing capability cannot be observed from the read-only assigned paths.

theories.claim: IsolationWorkspace.Run (isolation.go:158-183) enforces env validation (no NUL byte, must contain =) and applies nativeIsolationRequest only when Capabilities.NativeProtectedRootDeny is true; otherwise the request is passed through unchanged, leaving protected-root enforcement to the caller.
theories.basis: Cross-package contract between internal/platform/process.IsolationWorkspace.Run and the consumer (qa.go uses RunQAInvestigation with TargetRoot/WorkspaceParent/ProtectedRoots). Architecture says protected-root denial is the platform's responsibility and a missing capability must block writable work upstream.
theories.confirmation_condition: Run path checks Capabilities.NativeProtectedRootDeny before invoking nativeIsolationRequest and the request is forwarded unchanged otherwise, while env entries are rejected on NUL or missing =.
theories.refutation_condition: nativeIsolationRequest is always invoked regardless of capability, OR env validation is skipped.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Cannot observe behavior of nativeIsolationRequest or its absence from the read-only paths.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: grep -n "nativeIsolationRequest\|NativeProtectedRootDeny" internal/platform/process/*.go and read the function body.
theories.outcome_reason: Conditional bwrap application is textually present and architecture is consistent; the actual Linux behavior of nativeIsolationRequest cannot be exercised from read-only inspection.

theories.claim: handleSprintQAPage (qa_handlers.go:168-201) composes a pageModel that embeds Sprint, QA, QAShard, and QATheory DTOs; the page path is the only route that combines all four projections through the additive interface and is therefore the most surface-rich cross-package integration point.
theories.basis: Cross-package composition: handleSprintQAPage calls h.queries.Sprint (legacy surface), h.qa.QAStatus, and conditionally h.qa.QAShard and h.qa.QASynthesis-adjacent QATheory. The other handlers use a single projection each. Architecture says web must not decide workflow semantics and must not import sprint; the page route is the natural boundary test.
theories.confirmation_condition: handleSprintQAPage makes exactly four product calls (Sprint, QAStatus, optional QAShard, optional QATheory) and returns a single pageModel; no other handler aggregates that many projections.
theories.refutation_condition: Another handler aggregates the same four projections, OR the page path is split across multiple handlers.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Cannot inspect the html/template that consumes pageModel to confirm it does not require additional projections.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: grep -n "pageModel{\|h.queries\.Sprint\|h\.qa\." internal/web/qa_handlers.go internal/web/handlers.go to enumerate every projection request the page route performs.
theories.outcome_reason: Page composition shape is textually present and consistent with architecture; the template contract cannot be verified from these paths.

theories.claim: RunQA has two cross-package integration paths: the smoke suite short-circuit (qa.go:289-310) bypasses mutation context acquisition, qaMap construction, settings load, and writer fence injection, while the main path (qa.go:311-447) acquires the mutation lease, constructs the writer fence, and binds the store with WithWriterFence; the suite path therefore does not rely on isolation capabilities while the main path does.
theories.basis: Cross-package integration of sprint.RunQA with app.sprintRuntimeService (sprint_commands.go:754-780) which builds a controlled runtime and returns a Service bound to a controlled runtime and QA writer fence only on the main run path. Architecture says QA starts only after durable acceptance and owner claim; the smoke suite reuses the canonical smoke execution rather than copying it into a second runner (docs/architecture.md end of QA verification phase).
theories.confirmation_condition: Reading the two RunQA branches confirms the smoke path skips mutation context, qaMap load, store writer fence binding, and isolation capability probe, while the main path executes all of them.
theories.refutation_condition: The smoke path secretly enters the main path, OR the main path also runs the smoke suite, OR the writer fence is bound on the smoke path through a different mechanism.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Static reading cannot prove runtime sequence when qaCommand.Suite is empty versus smoke.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: grep -n "RunQA\|WithWriterFence\|acquireMutationContext\|RunSmoke" internal/sprint/qa.go internal/app/sprint_commands.go to enumerate every entry to RunQA and every fence binding site.
theories.outcome_reason: Branch separation is textually present and matches the architecture description of smoke reuse; whether any non-suite action still ends up in the suite branch cannot be determined without runtime.
